title: Soya bean scale on broad beans and pigeon peas

Header: Soya bean scale on broad beans and pigeon peas

Prevention: Remove any alternate host plants/ weeds from the area especially milkweed ( Euphorbia sp.)
The insect has a wide host range from vegetable crops to weed species and herbs.
This pest is now well established in
Monitoring: Look for all stages of insect life cycle, e.g. nymphs (crawlers), as well as ants that could indicate their presence.
Adult insect with an orange body and black legs with a white fluted egg sac or ovisac.
Egg sac held at a 45 degree angle to the plant stalk.
Eggs are pinkish and crawlers move around plant after hatching from the ovisac.
Direct Control: Syneura cocciphila ) attack the insect and they will reduce the populations but may be too late to save the crop and insecticide sprays may be required.
Restrictions: All the insecticides above have systemic activity.
Ensure that appropriate personal protective equipment is worn when using agro-chemicals.
Highly toxic to fish and bees
